solutions.latex:
$|2x-3|=9x$ means $2x-3=9x$ or $-(2x-3)=9x$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2x - 3 &= 9x & \qquad -2x + 3 &= 9x \\ -3 &= 7x & 3 &= 11x \\ x &= -\dfrac{3}{7} & x &= \dfrac{3}{11} \end{aligned}$$
Test the solutions in the original equation.

$x=-\dfrac{3}{7}$:
$$\left|2 \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{7}\right) - 3\right| = \dfrac{27}{7},\qquad 9 \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{7}\right)=-\dfrac{27}{7}$$
These are not equal, so $x = -\dfrac{3}{7}$ is not a solution.

$x=\dfrac{3}{11}$:
$$\left|2 \times \dfrac{3}{11} - 3\right| = \dfrac{27}{11},\qquad 9 \times \dfrac{3}{11}=\dfrac{27}{11}$$
These are equal.
$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{3}{11}$$

solutions.latex: \exfigure{373_q11_s1}

Graphically, the line $y=2x+4$ meets $y=|x-1|$ at $x=-1$ (the line must be sketched on the graph from part (a)).

Alternatively, solve algebraically in two cases.

Case 1, $x-1\ge0$, so $|x-1|=x-1$:
$$\begin{aligned} x-1&=2x+4 \\ -x&=5 \\ x&=-5 \end{aligned}$$
This does not satisfy $x\ge1$, so reject.

Case 2, $x-1<0$, so $|x-1|=-(x-1)=1-x$:
$$\begin{aligned} 1-x&=2x+4 \\ -3x&=3 \\ x&=-1 \end{aligned}$$
Check: $-1<1$, so this satisfies $x-1<0$.
$$\therefore x=-1$$

Substitute $x=0$, $y=6$:
$$\begin{aligned}6&=|b|\\ b&=\pm 6\end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
The $y$-intercept is $5$:
$$|0\cdot a+b|=5 \quad\Rightarrow\quad b=\pm5$$
The $x$-intercept is $2.5$, so $2.5a+b=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} b=-5:&\quad 2.5a=5,\ a=2 \\ b=5:&\quad 2.5a=-5,\ a=-2 \end{aligned}$$
Both give the same graph, since $|-2x+5|=|2x-5|$ (check the point $(2,1)$: $|2\times2-5|=1$).
$$\therefore\ a=2,\ b=-5\ \ (\text{or } a=-2,\ b=5)$$
